brief_problem: Who won at noughts and crosses?

runs.text: A matrix is an array with rows and columns, and each cell is found with two numbers.
At break they play noughts and crosses. When they finish, the board is written down row by row:
Decide who won with this board, written row by row: 1, 2, 1 / 2, 1, 2 / 2, 1, 1.
X wins, by the diagonal that goes from the top left corner to the bottom right one: the three cells hold 1.

inputs.text: nine numbers, row by row: 0 empty, 1 X and 2 O.

relation.text: whoever completes a row, a column or one of the two diagonals wins.

examples.text: the board in the task → X wins, by a diagonal.
a board without three in a row → nobody.

runs.text: There are eight ways to win: three rows, three columns and two diagonals. An empty cell does not win even if there are three in a row: the empty board is the edge case.

blocks.description: A 3 by 3 board with the row and the column written in each cell, from [0, 0] to [2, 2]. The two diagonals are highlighted: the one where the row equals the column and the one where row plus column equals 2.

caption.text: Each cell has a row and a column. On one diagonal the row equals the column; on the other, they add up to 2.

entries.text: Read the nine numbers into their cells.
Check each row, each column and the two diagonals: it is the search pattern, eight times.
If any has three equal, non-empty cells, whoever is in them won.

runs.text: is a two-dimensional array: each cell is found with two indices, the row and the column. Both start at 0.
